incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government bodies and state-owned energy operators
incidents.vector: ASPX web shells dropped on exploited public web applications, followed by SoftEther VPN/VNT tunneling, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato privilege escalation, and a new bespoke 'TinyRCT' .NET backdoor.
incidents.impact: Chinese-speaking operators tracked as CL-STA-1062 compromised at least ten Southeast Asian organizations, exfiltrating MSSQL databases and web-server source code and burrowing into two state-owned critical energy entities across a months-long campaign.

incidents.vector: An SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-20230) in the CUCM WebDialer service is chained to deploy a rogue Apache Axis service and a JSP web shell for root-level code execution.
incidents.impact: Attackers weaponized the bug within 24 hours of a public proof-of-concept; researchers observed mass scanning, and organizations with WebDialer exposed should assume compromise.

incidents.victim: Hotels and hospitality operators across Europe and Asia
incidents.vector: Phishing emails laundered through Calendly and Google redirect infrastructure deliver photo-themed ZIP archives whose fake image shortcuts launch obfuscated PowerShell and a Node.js implant with dual registry persistence.
incidents.impact: Microsoft has tracked an active multi-stage intrusion campaign against reception and front-desk staff since April 2026; post-compromise activity includes C2 beaconing and PE payload compilation, suggesting preparation for follow-on operations.

incidents.vector: USB drives pre-infected with Chinese malware were connected to classified military networks (supply-chain compromise).
incidents.impact: Japan's military used factory-infected USB devices on classified systems; the breach reportedly went undisclosed for about a year before being uncovered, and NATO partners are now being notified.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party mobile device management provider running Ivanti EPMM, tied to the prior year's wave of Ivanti EPMM server attacks.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officials were stolen via the breached MDM platform.

incidents.vector: Data theft and extortion by the group operating as 'World Leaks'.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed the theft of more than 200,000 documents, including sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.vector: Breach of a shared public email platform used by KDDI and several other Japanese ISPs.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to more than 14 million users was stolen from the KDDI-operated email service.

incidents.vector: Malicious code injected through a compromised third-party vendor.
incidents.impact: Roughly $3 million was stolen from the prediction-market platform before detection; Polymarket is reimbursing affected users.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment against the subsidiary's systems.
incidents.impact: A ransomware attack disrupted operations at the Indian automaker's engineering/research subsidiary, which disclosed the incident to market authorities.

incidents.vector: Network compromise (details not disclosed).
incidents.impact: The university is rebuilding its entire IT infrastructure following a hack.

incidents.vector: Network attack against mobile-app infrastructure, with the IT Army of Russia claiming an earlier database breach.
incidents.impact: Ukrposhta's mobile app and web services were knocked offline, disrupting operations across thousands of post offices; claimed data theft is unverified.

incidents.vector: Rogue SD-WAN peering and stolen certificate material gave SSH access, then a zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager was exploited via a malicious CSV upload to escalate to root.
incidents.impact: Mandiant found an actor who created a hidden root account ('troot'), exfiltrated SD-WAN fabric configurations, and used extensive anti-forensic cleanup to maintain stealthy control over the provider's central network plane.

incidents.victim: Global cybercrime victims (140,000+ infected computers in May alone)
incidents.vector: Amadey loader and StealC infostealer, sold as malware-as-a-service, were taken down via court orders and domain/server seizures.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, Europol and partners disrupted 200+ Amadey and StealC C2 domains/servers, severing control of over 18,000 victim machines; the same Amadey infrastructure had been abused by Russian state actors against Ukraine.

incidents.victim: Compromised WordPress sites and downstream ransomware victims
incidents.vector: The SocGholish botnet pushed malware disguised as software updates from thousands of hacked WordPress sites, providing access for follow-on ransomware.
incidents.impact: Operation Endgame seized 106 SocGholish servers/domains, and Dutch police removed backdoors from 14,971 WordPress sites; the operation has historically been linked to the Evil Corp cybercrime gang.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack against corporate IT systems (specifics undisclosed).
incidents.impact: Logistics and accounting operations were disrupted, forcing manual processing of shipments and paperwork while production continued.

incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing attack against user accounts using reused passwords.
incidents.impact: A Minnesota man known as 'Snoopy' was sentenced for a 2022 scheme that compromised ~60,000 DraftKings accounts, stole about $600,000 and resold access to tens of thousands of accounts.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (and U.S. healthcare victims)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized network intrusion and extortion by the English-speaking cybercrime crew known as Scattered Spider.
incidents.impact: Two UK nationals pleaded guilty over the August 2024 TfL attack; one, also wanted in the U.S., is tied to roughly 120 intrusions into 47 U.S. entities yielding at least $115 million in ransom.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Check Point Remote Access VPN
incidents.vector: A certificate-validation logic error (CVE-2026-50751) let unauthenticated attackers create VPN sessions on IKEv1-enabled gateways.
incidents.impact: A Qilin ransomware affiliate breached a few dozen organizations worldwide during a roughly six-week undetected window, using Rclone for exfiltration before a patch and CISA directive followed.

incidents.victim: North American medical, academic and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of externally facing REDCap research servers, custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest credentials, then abuse of Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: A PRC-nexus actor (UNC6508) remained undetected for over a year while pursuing defense, AI, uncrewed-systems and medical research data across multiple US and Canadian institutions; Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.victim: 73,932 FortiGate systems across 194 countries (government, defense, finance, healthcare)
incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of internet-exposed FortiGate firewalls to export configs and credentials, plus a custom 'FortigateSniffer' intercepting traffic across 24 protocols and offline GPU hash-cracking.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed 73,932 FortiGate admin/VPN credentials; a Russian-speaking access broker validated and resold access, with confirmed breaches including a Turkish NATO defense contractor whose classified documents were exfiltrated.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal agencies and enterprises running Oracle PeopleSoft
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-35273) in Oracle PeopleTools / PeopleSoft Enterprise.
incidents.impact: CISA added the actively exploited bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; successful post-exploitation grants total control of affected PeopleSoft assets.

incidents.victim: 1,000+ organizations across 47 U.S. states and 31 countries
incidents.vector: Conti ransomware encryption and data-theft extortion; the defendant helped develop the malware loader.
incidents.impact: A Ukrainian national extradited from Ireland pleaded guilty to wire-fraud conspiracy tied to the Conti operation, which extracted at least $150 million in ransom; sentencing is set for September 2026.
